assumptions: the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: MEASURED across all 17 receipts. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS shared the block. COPY: INV-R8.3, INV-R9 and INV-R9.1 each ship lineage.parent_ids [“INV-R8.1-CONCURRENCY-OBSERVED”] beside a `parent` field naming INV-R8.2, INV-R8.3 and INV-R9 respectively — wrong when written, carried forward by copy, and the chain starts at INV-R8.3, one round earlier than the audit that found it located it. Their `rollback_target` is stale by the same route, and INV-R9.1’s reconstruction still owes “INV-R7.1’s content, replayed onto this head” in the receipt of the round that integrated it. SNAPSHOT: four receipts list one unpromoted revision where the registry now holds five — each was CORRECT when written, and a snapshot of mutable state inside an immutable record is not at risk of going stale, it is guaranteed to, and under FAC-PROMOTION-FINALITY it cannot be repaired in place. The same rule reaches scope prose: three receipts say “Nothing else” beside a DERIVED tree_delta of 10, 9 and 8 paths. check-lineage §8 derives all of it, prints it, and from INV-R9.2 refuses a receipt carrying a derivable lineage field or stating its own scope in prose.
attrs.gap: THE PHRASE TEST IS A BACKSTOP AND THE WEAKER HALF, exactly as FAC-COUNT-DERIVED says of §7. Deciding whether a sentence states a scope is the same undecidable problem as deciding whether it states a cardinality; the four patterns matched here are the ones already observed. THE PRIMARY REPAIR IS REMOVAL — INV-R6.2’s ruling when `_round` became a pointer: there is no reason for a second account to exist, and render-and-compare would hide the duplicate rather than remove it. Second: the rule is ENFORCED_FROM INV-R9.2 and the earlier receipts keep their drift, because a new invariant cannot bind immutable history; nine notes print every run and none of them fails. THIRD, AND MEASURED ON THIS ROUND’S OWN RECEIPT: the phrase test cannot distinguish USE from MENTION. The first draft of INV-R9.2’s transition.candidate quoted INV-R9.1’s `Nothing else` in order to name the defect, and the gate refused it — correctly by its own rule and wrongly as a matter of meaning. The quotation moved to transition.why, which is not scanned. That is not a repair; it is where a pattern list stops, and it is the second reason the primary mechanism is REMOVAL of the field rather than matching of its contents.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9 audit §§9–10, which found the stale block on two receipts and the false transition sentence on one.
attrs.review_focus: The SNAPSHOT half generalises past receipts: any immutable record that embeds the current state of a mutable registry has this defect. Does the artifact hold others?
attrs.statement: A transition receipt keeps no second, independently writable account of its own ancestry or of its own scope. Parentage, rollback target, revision states and delta size are derived from the authoritative fields, the registry and the repository, and a receipt written under the rule may not carry them.
